utterances.text: I agree, you are a Bosnian and a Herzegovac, but again I think we're wandering outside of the subject. The fact is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, no. State, not national, because if it's national, then it belonged to the three officially-recognised nations, the Muslims, the Serbs and the Croats, irrespective of the order you take. It doesn't matter. Even the constitution changes the order; Serbs, Croats, Muslims; Muslims, Croats, Serbs, and so on and so forth. You know that constitution from the former Yugoslavia, the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so it was equally Serb, Croat and Muslim. Why would the Serbs then be interested in destroying this cultural treasure? In destroying the traces of Serb existence for almost a thousand years before the Turks came to Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the kind of traces that are there, from the Tartars of Kulin Ban and so on and so forth. Do you know about that? And do you know that anyone conducted a serious, impartial investigation about the burning down of the town hall? Have you ever heard of anything like that? Just say "yes" or "no," please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the International Court of Justice, which in its judgement in the case Bosnia-Herzegovina versus Serbian Montenegro, made very few rulings on facts. Most of the facts it relied upon were from the judgements of the ICTY, but on this one they ruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you at this point. The International Court of Justice never conducted any kind of investigation. They heard witnesses that were called by the two opposing parties, but they did not conduct an investigation. No one conducted an objective, impartial investigation, because all the Western observers in Sarajevo knew straight away what this was all about. Had they had any suspicion that it was done by the Serbs, they would have carried out an investigation in order to brand this as barbarism. Since they knew it was the Muslims who did this, there was no investigation, not by the Council of Europe, not by the UN, no one; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we're going to have to put an end to this. Mr. Seselj's argument is that the disappearance of these books, these works, important works for the three important components, elements of Bosnia-Herzegovina is, according to him, due to the Muslims and not to the Serbs. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe there is no credible evidence to support that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the Registrar shall tell me now how much time Mr. Seselj has yet. You have 26 minutes left, Mr. Seselj, for tomorrow, after deduction. So tomorrow, we will resume our hearing at a quarter past 2.00. Mr. Seselj will have the floor for 26 minutes, after which maybe Mr. Mundis may wish to redirect. And if there are no questions after that, we will thank the witness, who may withdraw. I was very optimistic, Witness, at the beginning of this hearing. I was hoping we might finish today, but unfortunately we still need 30 minutes. So you may stay until tomorrow; is it possible for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. My wife will be unhappy, but I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore, you will apologise for us to your wife, but in the interests of justice we need you to be here tomorrow. Therefore, please convey my regrets to your wife, and we meet again tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of May, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
